title: IBM Watson for Oncology MD Anderson partnership failure
system_purpose: Assist oncologists in identifying suitable cancer treatment options
decision_impact: System recommendations influenced treatment plans for cancer patients at MD Anderson Cancer Center
verified_facts: MD Anderson invested approximately $62 million over five years. The pilot was discontinued in 2018 after failing to meet its goals. Watson was trained on synthetic cases rather than real patient data, limiting generalization to diverse populations.
reported_harm: Risk of incorrect cancer treatment recommendations due to training data that did not reflect real-world clinical diversity. The mismatch between AI recommendations and physician expertise created potential for patient confusion and suboptimal treatment decisions.
quantitative_evidence: $62 million MD Anderson investment. $4 billion development cost. $1 billion sale price in 2022. Discontinued partnership after 5 years.
limitations: Patient-level outcome data is not publicly available. The failure was documented through financial losses rather than specific patient harm cases. The case reflects enterprise AI adoption challenges including unrealistic expectations and insufficient training data quality.

title: Theranos fraudulent blood testing technology
system_purpose: Provide comprehensive blood testing from minimal finger prick samples
decision_impact: Test results influenced patient medical decisions about diagnoses and medication dosing
affected_groups: patients who received Theranos blood test results
verified_facts: A 2016 quality review found 68% of lab measurements showed significant variability compared to reference standards. Lipid panel results were non-equivalent to standard testing. The company voided two years of Edison test results. FDA inspections revealed nanotainers were uncleared medical devices.
reported_harm: Direct patient harm: patients made medical decisions based on incorrect test results. Warfarin dosing errors could cause life-threatening bleeding or blood clots. Two years of voided results meant thousands of patients received erroneous information.
quantitative_evidence: 68% of lab measurements showed significant variability. Two years of test results voided. Elizabeth Holmes sentenced to 11 years 3 months prison.
limitations: While Theranos was primarily a physical device and fraud case rather than an AI system, it demonstrates critical lessons about insufficient regulatory oversight and the importance of independent validation. These lessons apply to AI health applications.

title: Racial and socioeconomic bias in clinical decision support algorithms
system_purpose: Support clinical decision-making for patient triage and care recommendations
decision_impact: Algorithm recommendations influenced care levels and resource allocation affecting patient access
affected_groups: Black and Hispanic patients. Low-income populations. Elderly patients. Rural populations.
verified_facts: Clinical decision support algorithms used race as a variable in ways that perpetuated existing healthcare disparities. Historical data used to train models reflected systemic inequities. When algorithms learned from this data, they encoded these biases as normal patterns.
reported_harm: Delayed or reduced access to appropriate care for minority patients due to algorithmic recommendations that reflected historical discrimination rather than patient need. The bias was often invisible to clinicians using the system.
quantitative_evidence: Multiple academic studies documented algorithmic bias in healthcare settings. Pew Research found 60% of Americans are concerned about bias in healthcare AI.
limitations: Most documented bias cases are from US healthcare systems with different demographic compositions than Vietnam. The fundamental risk of bias in AI trained on historical data is universal and applies regardless of geographic context.
